title: Packet Switching & Routing
summary: Model packet structure (Header, Payload, Footer) and run an unplugged whole-class Packet Relay simulation to prove how out-of-order packets reassemble reliably.

slidesBlueprint.contentSummary: Groups of 5 act as Sender, 3 Routers, and Receiver. Sender splits a 4-word phrase onto 4 slips with sequence numbers and sends via different desk routes while one router is blocked.

pedagogicalRationale.cognitiveLoadNote: Physical roles externalise memory steps so every pupil grasps why sequence numbers are essential.

slidesData.title: Inside a Data Packet

customCanvasElements.heading: 1. Header
customCanvasElements.content:
• Holds Sender IP and Destination IP.
• Lists Sequence number (e.g. 2 of 3) to rebuild order.

customCanvasElements.heading: 2. Payload
customCanvasElements.content:
• Holds the actual chunk of data (~1,500 bytes).
• Could be part of a photo, video, or message.

customCanvasElements.heading: 3. Trailer
customCanvasElements.content:
• Runs an error check called a Checksum.
• Asks to resend the packet if bits get corrupted.

slidesData.title: Unplugged Packet Relay

bodyBlocks.heading: 1. Split & Address
bodyBlocks.content:
• Write a 4-word message across 4 slips.
• Add To, From, Sequence (1/4–4/4), and a letter-count Checksum.

bodyBlocks.heading: 2. Route Around Failure
bodyBlocks.content:
• Send packets 10 seconds apart across different desks.
• Switch paths if a desk is marked offline.

bodyBlocks.heading: 3. Reassemble & Check
bodyBlocks.content:
• Receiver sorts slips 1 to 4 and checks letter counts.
• Send a "Resend" slip back if any packet is wrong.

slidesData.speakerNotes: Playful active task! Intentionally intercept Packet 2 from one group and secretly change a letter to test if the Receiver catches the checksum mismatch.

pedagogicalBadges.cognitiveLoadNote: Physical roleplay embeds sequence numbers & checksums far better than passive copying.

bodyBlocks.heading: In Your Books
bodyBlocks.content:
• Why do packets sometimes arrive out of order?
• Which part of the packet fixes the order?
• What happens if one packet arrives corrupted?
